title: The type of a numerical semigroup has the parity of its Frobenius number half the time (Singhal's Conjecture 7.2)
source: Deepesh Singhal, “Numerical Semigroups of small and large type”, arXiv:2008.08110 (2020), Conjecture 7.2. https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.08110
statement:
Let $F(S)$ be the Frobenius number of a numerical semigroup $S$, let $t(S)$ be its type, and let the denominator count all numerical semigroups with Frobenius number $F$. **Frobenius type-parity equidistribution conjecture.**

$$
\lim_{F\to\infty}\frac{\#\{S\mid F(S)=F,\ t(S)\equiv F\pmod{2}\}}{\#\{S\mid F(S)=F\}}=\frac{1}{2}.
$$

The conjecture is motivated by the same numerical data for $F\leq 30$ and predicts asymptotic equidistribution of the two type parities relative to the parity of $F$.
summary: The conjecture holds: among numerical semigroups with Frobenius number F, the proportion whose type has the same parity as F tends to 1/2 as F grows, along all F. Almost all such semigroups have multiplicity close to F/2 (Backelin 1990; the one-sided form needed is proved here). For those, adding or removing the single element ⌊3F/4⌋ gives another numerical semigroup with the same Frobenius number, and the toggle changes the parity of the type unless the semigroup has pseudo-Frobenius numbers at one of a few small gaps from that element; a greedy count of disjoint pairs shows that the exceptional semigroups form a vanishing fraction. So the semigroups pair up, outside a negligible set, into pairs of opposite type parity. Lean defines numerical semigroups as cofinite additive submonoids of ℕ containing 0, the Frobenius number, the pseudo-Frobenius numbers and the type, and proves that the ratio of cardinalities tends to 1/2, both for the sets themselves and for a finite encoding used in the proof.
paste_summary: Proved. Singhal (arXiv:2008.08110, Conjecture 7.2) conjectured that among numerical semigroups with Frobenius number F the proportion whose type is congruent to F modulo 2 tends to 1/2. Toggling the element ⌊3F/4⌋ pairs almost all such semigroups into pairs of opposite type parity; the exceptions are shown to be a vanishing fraction.
caveat: The limit is along all F, as in Conjecture 7.2 (the neighbouring Conjecture 7.3 concerns residue classes and is not addressed). The concentration of multiplicity near F/2 is due to Backelin (1990); Lean proves the one-sided estimate it needs and does not assume Backelin's theorem. The written proof by Claude Opus needed a local correction to a floor inequality found by the GPT-6.2 Sol review. The journal version of the source was not read (reviewer's probability that it settles the conjecture: 0.02); ProbXiv and the arXiv keyword API were unavailable. Proof and first (same-model) review are by Claude Opus 5.5 (the same-model review had rated it 0.5); the cross-model review (not routine 0.68), the Lean code and the final check (a separate lane) are by GPT-6.2 Sol, so the final check is by the same model family as the Lean packager.
